connection_profile_id.description: The ID of the connection profile.
connection_profile_id.rationale: Connection Profile ID has no impact on the security of the resource or data contained

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls Terraform deletion behaviour for the connection profile resource. It does not directly configure database access, encryption, networking, or authentication.

display_name.rationale: Display name has no impact on the security of the resource or data contained

labels.description:
The resource labels for connection profile to use to annotate any related underlying resources such as Compute Engine VMs.


**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Labels have no impact on the security of the resource or data contained

location.description: The location where the connection profile should reside.
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

role.description: The connection profile role. Possible values: ["SOURCE", "DESTINATION"]
role.rationale: Defines whether the profile is used as a source or destination. It controls migration role selection, not a direct security enforcement mechanism.

alloydb.description: Specifies required connection parameters, and the parameters required to create an AlloyDB destination cluster.
alloydb.rationale: Container block for AlloyDB connection settings. Security decisions are made by its nested fields rather than this block itself.

alloydb.cluster_id.description: Required. The AlloyDB cluster ID that this connection profile is associated with.

alloydb.settings.description: Immutable. Metadata used to create the destination AlloyDB cluster.
alloydb.settings.rationale: Container block for AlloyDB settings. Security impact is determined by the specific nested configuration fields.

alloydb.settings.labels.description: Labels for the AlloyDB cluster created by DMS.
alloydb.settings.labels.rationale: Labels are metadata for organisation and filtering. They do not directly configure access, encryption, networking, or authentication.

alloydb.settings.vpc_network.description:
Required. The resource link for the VPC network in which cluster resources are created and from which they are accessible via Private IP. The network must belong to the same project as the cluster.
It is specified in the form: 'projects/{project_number}/global/networks/{network_id}'. This is required to create a cluster.
alloydb.settings.vpc_network.rationale: References the VPC network the AlloyDB cluster peers with. This is a pointer to another resource chosen by the team; we do not constrain the names of networks the resource merely references, so it is not a policy target.

alloydb.settings.initial_user.description: Required. Input only. Initial user to setup during cluster creation.
alloydb.settings.initial_user.rationale: Container block for initial AlloyDB user details. The nested username and password fields carry the relevant meaning.

alloydb.settings.initial_user.password.description: The initial password for the user.
alloydb.settings.initial_user.password.rationale: Stores an initial database password value for provisioning. Secret handling is security-sensitive operationally, but this field is not a policy-enforceable configuration choice in this resource.

alloydb.settings.initial_user.user.rationale: Defines the initial database username. It is an identity label for provisioning and does not by itself grant permissions or enforce a security control.

alloydb.settings.primary_instance_settin.description: Settings for the cluster's primary instance
alloydb.settings.primary_instance_settin.rationale: Container block for AlloyDB primary instance settings. Security impact is determined by specific nested settings.

alloydb.settings.primary_instance_settin.description: Database flags to pass to AlloyDB when DMS is creating the AlloyDB cluster and instances. See the AlloyDB documentation for how these can be used.
alloydb.settings.primary_instance_settin.rationale: Database flags tune AlloyDB instance behaviour. This generic map can affect runtime configuration but is not a single direct security control in this policy set.
Identifies the primary AlloyDB instance created by DMS. It is a resource identifier rather than a direct security control.

alloydb.settings.primary_instance_settin.description: Labels for the AlloyDB primary instance created by DMS.
alloydb.settings.primary_instance_settin.rationale: Labels are metadata for the AlloyDB primary instance and do not directly enforce security behaviour.

alloydb.settings.primary_instance_settin.description: Configuration for the machines that host the underlying database engine.
alloydb.settings.primary_instance_settin.rationale: Container block for machine sizing settings. CPU count affects capacity rather than directly enforcing a security control.

alloydb.settings.primary_instance_settin.description: The number of CPU's in the VM instance.
alloydb.settings.primary_instance_settin.rationale: Sets compute capacity for the AlloyDB primary instance. It affects sizing and performance, not direct security enforcement.

cloudsql.description: Specifies required connection parameters, and, optionally, the parameters required to create a Cloud SQL destination database instance.
cloudsql.rationale: Container block for Cloud SQL connection settings. Security decisions are made by its nested fields rather than this block itself.

cloudsql.settings.description: Immutable. Metadata used to create the destination Cloud SQL database.
cloudsql.settings.rationale: Container block for Cloud SQL settings. Security impact is determined by the specific nested configuration fields.

cloudsql.settings.activation_policy.description: The activation policy specifies when the instance is activated; it is applicable only when the instance state is 'RUNNABLE'. Possible values: ["ALWAYS", "NEVER"]

cloudsql.settings.auto_storage_increase.description:
If you enable this setting, Cloud SQL checks your available storage every 30 seconds. If the available storage falls below a threshold size, Cloud SQL automatically adds additional storage capacity.
If the available storage repeatedly falls below the threshold size, Cloud SQL continues to add storage until it reaches the maximum of 30 TB.

cloudsql.settings.cmek_key_name.description: The KMS key name used for the csql instance.
cloudsql.settings.cmek_key_name.rationale: CloudSQL connection profiles must use CMEK encryption.

cloudsql.settings.collation.description: The Cloud SQL default instance level collation.

cloudsql.settings.data_disk_size_gb.description: The storage capacity available to the database, in GB. The minimum (and default) size is 10GB.

cloudsql.settings.data_disk_type.description: The type of storage. Possible values: ["PD_SSD", "PD_HDD"]

cloudsql.settings.database_flags.description: The database flags passed to the Cloud SQL instance at startup.
cloudsql.settings.database_flags.rationale: Database flags tune Cloud SQL instance behaviour. This generic map can affect runtime configuration but is not a single direct security control in this policy set.

cloudsql.settings.database_version.description:
The database engine type and version.
Currently supported values located at https://cloud.google.com/database-migration/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.connectionProfiles#sqldatabaseversion

cloudsql.settings.edition.description: The edition of the given Cloud SQL instance. Possible values: ["ENTERPRISE", "ENTERPRISE_PLUS"]

cloudsql.settings.source_id.description: The Database Migration Service source connection profile ID, in the format: projects/my_project_name/locations/us-central1/connectionProfiles/connection_profile_ID

cloudsql.settings.storage_auto_resize_li.description: The maximum size to which storage capacity can be automatically increased. The default value is 0, which specifies that there is no limit.

cloudsql.settings.tier.description:
The tier (or machine type) for this instance, for example: db-n1-standard-1 (MySQL instances) or db-custom-1-3840 (PostgreSQL instances).
For more information, see https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql/instance-settings

cloudsql.settings.user_labels.description: The resource labels for a Cloud SQL instance to use to annotate any related underlying resources such as Compute Engine VMs.

cloudsql.settings.zone.description: The Google Cloud Platform zone where your Cloud SQL datdabse instance is located.

cloudsql.settings.ip_config.description: The settings for IP Management. This allows to enable or disable the instance IP and manage which external networks can connect to the instance. The IPv4 address cannot be disabled.
cloudsql.settings.ip_config.rationale: Container block for Cloud SQL IP configuration. Security decisions are represented by nested network fields such as SSL, private network, and authorized networks.

cloudsql.settings.ip_config.enable_ipv4.description: Whether the instance should be assigned an IPv4 address or not.

cloudsql.settings.ip_config.private_netw.description:
The resource link for the VPC network from which the Cloud SQL instance is accessible for private IP. For example, projects/myProject/global/networks/default.
This setting can be updated, but it cannot be removed after it is set.
cloudsql.settings.ip_config.private_netw.rationale: Private networks restrict connectivity to internal VPCs, preventing exposure over the public internet.

cloudsql.settings.ip_config.require_ssl.description: Whether SSL connections over IP should be enforced or not.
cloudsql.settings.ip_config.require_ssl.rationale: Enforcing SSL ensures that all traffic between clients and the database is encrypted

cloudsql.settings.ip_config.authorized_n.description: The list of external networks that are allowed to connect to the instance using the IP.
cloudsql.settings.ip_config.authorized_n.rationale: Container block for authorized network entries. The actual security decision is the nested network value.

cloudsql.settings.ip_config.authorized_n.description: The time when this access control entry expires in RFC 3339 format.
cloudsql.settings.ip_config.authorized_n.rationale: Sets when an authorized-network entry expires. It supports lifecycle control, but the security boundary is the authorized network value itself.

cloudsql.settings.ip_config.authorized_n.description: A label to identify this entry.
cloudsql.settings.ip_config.authorized_n.rationale: Labels an authorized-network entry for identification. It does not directly grant or restrict access.

cloudsql.settings.ip_config.authorized_n.description: Input only. The time-to-leave of this access control entry.
cloudsql.settings.ip_config.authorized_n.rationale: Sets the lifetime of an authorized-network entry. It supports lifecycle control, but the security boundary is the authorized network value itself.

cloudsql.settings.ip_config.authorized_n.description: The allowlisted value for the access control list.
cloudsql.settings.ip_config.authorized_n.rationale: Defines the external network range allowed to connect to the Cloud SQL instance. Overly broad values can expose the database to untrusted networks.

mysql.description: Specifies connection parameters required specifically for MySQL databases.
mysql.rationale: Container block for MySQL connection settings. Security impact is determined by nested SSL and credential fields.

mysql.cloud_sql_id.description: If the connection profile is a Cloud SQL database, use this field to provide the Cloud SQL instance ID.
mysql.cloud_sql_id.rationale: cloud_sql_id has no impact on the security of the resource or data contained

mysql.host.description: The IP or hostname of the source MySQL database.
mysql.host.rationale: host value itself does not impact security since networking and SSL enforcement are controlled by other parameters such as private_network and require_ssl.

mysql.password.description:
Input only. The password for the user that Database Migration Service will be using to connect to the database.
This field is not returned on request, and the value is encrypted when stored in Database Migration Service.
mysql.password.rationale: Holds the source-database credential for the connection profile. It is a free-form secret value supplied per team/database; a platform policy cannot enforce strength or rotation on it and must never pin a specific value, so it is not a useful policy target.

mysql.port.description: The network port of the source MySQL database.
mysql.port.rationale: Port has no impact on the security since the host will be private

mysql.username.description: The username that Database Migration Service will use to connect to the database. The value is encrypted when stored in Database Migration Service.
mysql.username.rationale: Username has no impact on the security of the resource or data contained

mysql.ssl.description: SSL configuration for the destination to connect to the source database.
mysql.ssl.rationale: Container block for MySQL SSL settings. The SSL mode field controls the security behaviour.

mysql.ssl.ca_certificate.description:
Input only. The x509 PEM-encoded certificate of the CA that signed the source database server's certificate.
The replica will use this certificate to verify it's connecting to the right host.
mysql.ssl.ca_certificate.rationale: Provides CA certificate material for SSL verification. It supports encrypted connectivity but is credential material rather than a policy decision in this resource.

mysql.ssl.client_certificate.description:
Input only. The x509 PEM-encoded certificate that will be used by the replica to authenticate against the source database server.
If this field is used then the 'clientKey' field is mandatory
mysql.ssl.client_certificate.rationale: Provides client certificate material for SSL authentication. It is sensitive credential material rather than a policy decision in this resource.

mysql.ssl.client_key.description:
Input only. The unencrypted PKCS#1 or PKCS#8 PEM-encoded private key associated with the Client Certificate.
If this field is used then the 'clientCertificate' field is mandatory.
mysql.ssl.client_key.rationale: Provides the private key for client certificate authentication. It is sensitive credential material and should be protected, but the policy decision is the SSL mode.

mysql.ssl.type.description: The current connection profile state. Possible values: ["SERVER_ONLY", "SERVER_CLIENT", "REQUIRED", "NONE"]
mysql.ssl.type.rationale: Controls the SSL mode used for MySQL connectivity. Weak or disabled SSL can expose database migration traffic to interception.

oracle.description: Specifies connection parameters required specifically for Oracle databases.
oracle.rationale: Container block for Oracle connection settings. Security impact is determined by nested connectivity and SSL fields.

oracle.database_service.description: Required. Database service for the Oracle connection.
oracle.database_service.rationale: Database service has no impact on the security of the resource or data contained

oracle.host.description: Required. The IP or hostname of the source Oracle database.
oracle.host.rationale: host value itself does not impact security since networking and SSL enforcement are controlled by other parameters.

oracle.password.description:
Required. Input only. The password for the user that Database Migration Service will be using to connect to the database.
This field is not returned on request, and the value is encrypted when stored in Database Migration Service.
oracle.password.rationale: Password is handled securely by GCP. Policy cannot enforce complexity.

oracle.port.description: Required. The network port of the source Oracle database.
oracle.port.rationale: Port has no impact on the security since the host will be private

oracle.username.description: Required. The username that Database Migration Service will use to connect to the database. The value is encrypted when stored in Database Migration Service.
oracle.username.rationale: Username alone has no security effect unless paired with weak roles.

oracle.forward_ssh_connectivity.description: SSL configuration for the destination to connect to the source database.
oracle.forward_ssh_connectivity.rationale: Container block for Oracle SSH connectivity details. Security impact is determined by specific nested host and credential fields.

oracle.forward_ssh_connectivity.hostname.description: Required. Hostname for the SSH tunnel.
oracle.forward_ssh_connectivity.hostname.rationale: Defines the SSH tunnel endpoint used for Oracle connectivity. An incorrect or unapproved host can route migration traffic through an unsafe destination.

oracle.forward_ssh_connectivity.password.description: Input only. SSH password. Only one of 'password' and 'private_key' can be configured.
oracle.forward_ssh_connectivity.password.rationale: Provides SSH password material. It is sensitive credential material and should be protected, but it is not a policy decision in this resource.

oracle.forward_ssh_connectivity.port.description: Port for the SSH tunnel, default value is 22.
oracle.forward_ssh_connectivity.port.rationale: Defines the SSH tunnel port. It affects connection routing but is not by itself a direct security control.

oracle.forward_ssh_connectivity.private_.description: Input only. SSH private key. Only one of 'password' and 'private_key' can be configured.
oracle.forward_ssh_connectivity.private_.rationale: Provides SSH private key material. It is sensitive credential material and should be protected, but it is not a policy decision in this resource.

oracle.forward_ssh_connectivity.username.description: Required. Username for the SSH tunnel.
oracle.forward_ssh_connectivity.username.rationale: Defines the SSH username used for tunnel authentication. It identifies the account but does not by itself enforce a security control.

oracle.private_connectivity.description: Configuration for using a private network to communicate with the source database
oracle.private_connectivity.rationale: Container block for Oracle private connectivity settings. The nested private connection field carries the security decision.

oracle.private_connectivity.private_conn.description: Required. The resource name (URI) of the private connection.
oracle.private_connectivity.private_conn.rationale: Defines the private connection used to reach the Oracle database. Requiring private connectivity reduces exposure to public network paths.

oracle.ssl.description: SSL configuration for the destination to connect to the source database.
oracle.ssl.rationale: Container block for Oracle SSL material. Specific certificate, key, and SSL mode fields carry the relevant meaning.

oracle.ssl.ca_certificate.description:
Input only. The x509 PEM-encoded certificate of the CA that signed the source database server's certificate.
The replica will use this certificate to verify it's connecting to the right host.
oracle.ssl.ca_certificate.rationale: Provides CA certificate material for SSL verification. It supports encrypted connectivity but is credential material rather than a policy decision in this resource.

oracle.ssl.client_certificate.description:
Input only. The x509 PEM-encoded certificate that will be used by the replica to authenticate against the source database server.
If this field is used then the 'clientKey' field is mandatory
oracle.ssl.client_certificate.rationale: Provides client certificate material for SSL authentication. It is sensitive credential material rather than a policy decision in this resource.

oracle.ssl.client_key.description:
Input only. The unencrypted PKCS#1 or PKCS#8 PEM-encoded private key associated with the Client Certificate.
If this field is used then the 'clientCertificate' field is mandatory.
oracle.ssl.client_key.rationale: Provides the private key for client certificate authentication. It is sensitive credential material and should be protected, but it is not a policy decision in this resource.

oracle.static_service_ip_connectivity.description:
This object has no nested fields.

Static IP address connectivity configured on service project.
oracle.static_service_ip_connectivity.rationale: Container block for Oracle static service IP connectivity. It does not directly enforce a security control by itself.

postgresql.description: Specifies connection parameters required specifically for PostgreSQL databases.
postgresql.rationale: Container block for PostgreSQL connection settings. Security impact is determined by nested connectivity and SSL fields.

postgresql.alloydb_cluster_id.description: If the connection profile is an AlloyDB instance, use this field to provide the AlloyDB cluster ID.
postgresql.alloydb_cluster_id.rationale: Alloydb cluster ID has no impact on the security of the resource or data contained

postgresql.cloud_sql_id.description: If the connection profile is a Cloud SQL database, use this field to provide the Cloud SQL instance ID.
postgresql.cloud_sql_id.rationale: cloud_sql_id has no impact on the security of the resource or data contained

postgresql.database.description: The name of the specific database within the host.
postgresql.database.rationale: Identifies the PostgreSQL database within the host. It is a database selector rather than a direct security control.

postgresql.host.description: The IP or hostname of the source MySQL database.
postgresql.host.rationale: host value itself does not impact security since networking and SSL enforcement are controlled by other parameters such as private_network and require_ssl.

postgresql.password.description:
Input only. The password for the user that Database Migration Service will be using to connect to the database.
This field is not returned on request, and the value is encrypted when stored in Database Migration Service.
postgresql.password.rationale: Password is handled securely by GCP. Policy cannot enforce complexity.

postgresql.port.description: The network port of the source MySQL database.
postgresql.port.rationale: Port number itself does not impact security if host is private.

postgresql.username.description: The username that Database Migration Service will use to connect to the database. The value is encrypted when stored in Database Migration Service.
postgresql.username.rationale: Username alone has no security effect unless paired with weak roles.

postgresql.private_connectivity.rationale: Container block for PostgreSQL private connectivity settings. The nested private connection field carries the relevant meaning.

postgresql.private_connectivity.private_.description: Required. The resource name (URI) of the private connection.
postgresql.private_connectivity.private_.rationale: Defines a private connection for PostgreSQL connectivity. This can reduce network exposure, but this branch does not currently include a policy for this field.

postgresql.ssl.description: SSL configuration for the destination to connect to the source database.
postgresql.ssl.rationale: Container block for PostgreSQL SSL settings. The SSL mode field controls the security behaviour.

postgresql.ssl.ca_certificate.description:
Input only. The x509 PEM-encoded certificate of the CA that signed the source database server's certificate.
The replica will use this certificate to verify it's connecting to the right host.
postgresql.ssl.ca_certificate.rationale: Provides CA certificate material for SSL verification. It supports encrypted connectivity but is credential material rather than a policy decision in this resource.

postgresql.ssl.client_certificate.description:
Input only. The x509 PEM-encoded certificate that will be used by the replica to authenticate against the source database server.
If this field is used then the 'clientKey' field is mandatory
postgresql.ssl.client_certificate.rationale: Provides client certificate material for SSL authentication. It is sensitive credential material rather than a policy decision in this resource.

postgresql.ssl.client_key.description:
Input only. The unencrypted PKCS#1 or PKCS#8 PEM-encoded private key associated with the Client Certificate.
If this field is used then the 'clientCertificate' field is mandatory.
postgresql.ssl.client_key.rationale: Provides the private key for client certificate authentication. It is sensitive credential material and should be protected, but the policy decision is the SSL mode.

postgresql.ssl.type.description: The current connection profile state. Possible values: ["SERVER_ONLY", "SERVER_CLIENT", "REQUIRED", "NONE"]
postgresql.ssl.type.rationale: Controls the SSL mode used for PostgreSQL connectivity. Weak or disabled SSL can expose database migration traffic to interception.
